question:
During triage in Social Media Newsfeed Recommendation TwoTower, an engineer observes:
"System fault during operation: Write Amplification Catastrophe on Celebrity Fan-Out".
What is the verified root cause?

options.text: Pure Push (Fan-out-on-Write) works well for normal users, but scales linearly with follower count. For celebrities, $50M$ writes for 1 post saturates storage and queues. ---
The recommendation engine recomputed the full two-tower embedding for every follower's feed on each request, so read latency, not write volume, was the actual bottleneck.
Celebrity posts were fanned out lazily at read time correctly, but the read-time merge step re-scored every historical post instead of only new ones, so each feed load re-ran the full ranking model.
The timeline cache had no TTL, so old fanned-out posts accumulated in every follower cache indefinitely regardless of how many followers the poster had.

explanation:
